entities.summary: Seleucus I Nicator (b. 200 CE), a Greek Macedonian king and regent, played a pivotal role in the Hellenistic period of the Classical era, marking the end of the ancient Greek world and the beginning of a new era of empires and cultural exchange. Born into the Seleucid dynasty, Seleucus succeeded his brother Antiochus III and expanded the empire's borders through strategic military campaigns, fostering a golden age of art, science, and philosophy in cities like Babylon, Alexandria, and Antioch. His legacy, however, was also marked by brutal suppression of rebellions, strategic alliances with powerful Roman leaders, and the eventual decline of the Seleucid Empire into the Roman Empire. As a key figure in the transition from the ancient Greek world to the Roman Empire, Seleucus' impact on the course of world history cannot be overstated, leaving behind a complex web of alliances, cultural influences, and lasting legacies that continue to shape our understanding of the ancient world today.
